facts.fact_text: On 2 April 2011 the first applicant attended an unauthorised opposition demonstration held at Fountains Square in Baku.
On 2 April 2011 the second applicant attended an unauthorised opposition demonstration held at Fountains Square in Baku.
The demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 was intended to be peaceful.
The demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
Upon arriving at Fountains Square at around 3 p.m. on 2 April 2011, the first applicant was arrested by police officers.

At around 2 p.m. on 2 April 2011, while the second applicant was chanting during the demonstration at Fountains Square, four police officers approached him and twisted his arms behind his back in order to put him in a police car.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the first applicant under Article 310.1 (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Nasimi district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case on the grounds that the first applicant's beating by S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) had not been proved.

The Nasimi district prosecutor's office mainly relied on the findings of an inquiry conducted by the Nasimi district prosecutor's office into a similar complaint of ill-treatment from M.H., who had been detained with the first applicant on 2 April 2011.
Police officer V.M. stated that the first applicant had not been detained in the temporary detention facility and had not been beaten.
In an appeal of 31 May 2011 filed with the Nasimi District Court against the decision to refuse to open a criminal case, the first applicant reiterated his previous complaints.
By a decision of 5 May 2011, the Sabail district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case regarding the second applicant's alleged ill-treatment.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office found that there was no evidence that the second applicant had been beaten by police during his arrest.

In his complaint to the Sabail District Court, the second applicant complained that the Sabail district prosecutor's office had failed to conduct an effective investigation into his ill-treatment complaints.

In his complaint to the Sabail District Court, the second applicant pointed out that the Sabail district prosecutor's office had relied on the testimonies of witnesses who had denied that S.N. had twisted his arms, while the photos he had submitted proved the contrary.
